newsitem.title: USA: ADM ex-officials to go on trial May 1998.
newsitem.headline: ADM ex-officials to go on trial May 1998.

text.p: The criminal trial of three former Archer Daniels Midland Co executives on price-fixing charges will begin May 1, 1998, a U.S. federal court said on Wednesday.

The date was set at a hearing before U.S. District Court Judge Blanche Manning, who is presiding over the case against Michael Andreas, former vice chairman of ADM and son of Chairman Dwayne Andreas; Terrance Wilson, former ADM group vice president, and Mark Whitacre, who had headed ADM's BioProducts division.
Late last year, the three men were indicted on charges of conspiring to fix the price of lysine, a feed additive. They have pleaded not guilty to the charges.
ADM, a leading agricultural products processor, pleaded guilty last year to fixing prices of lysine and citric acid -- a food additive -- and paid a record $100 million in fines.
While ADM is not involved in the criminal proceedings against the three former executives, it remains a defendant in a separate civil case involving high fructose corn syrup.

In that case, being heard in U.S. District Court for the Central Distict of Illinois, ADM is being sued by food and beverage companies for allegedly overcharging them. Other defendants include the A.E. Staley Manufacturing Co, a unit of Tate & Lyle Plc, Cargill Co and American Maize Products Co.
In the civil case, plaintiffs are seeking access to video and audio tapes that were part of the U.S. Justice Department's undercover investigation of ADM and several other companies.
Judge Michael Mihm has ordered the U.S. Justice Department to turn over the tapes. The department, however, is seeking to appeal the order.
In addition, Michael Andreas and Wilson also have sought to block release of the tapes on the grounds they may have an impact on the criminal proceedings against them.

Mihm has ordered the Justice Department to turn over the tapes to plaintiffs in the civil case because portions had already been shown to a special committee of ADM's board when it was negotiating a plea agreement with federal officials.
